top.title: Nwifuru is silently taking Ebonyi to greater heights, and touching every sector
top.description: By Anayo Okoli The trending is narrative given to the public in and outside Ebonyi State by opposition is that Governor Francis Nwifuru is not working. And this narrative has gained currency among the people. But a visit to the state indicates that indeed the contrary is the case. The Governor is indeed doing working and touching every sector of development. The reality on ground is that a lot of development is happening in the State. Across the 13 local government areas of thespian state, no community is left out, at least with a road project. According to records, on assumption of office, Governor Francis Nwifuru unfolded what he called “People’s Charter of Needs” as a priority guide to his development trajectory and his administration has followed this religiously. In fact some of the ongoing projects are landmark projects that would project the state to national and even international maps. For instance, two specialized universities being built by the government will change the education landscape of the State. One of them, the ICT University has taken off at a temporary site with over 100 students receiving education free of charge. Work at the permanent site in Oferekpe, located in a vast land space, is ongoing with many sections, including lecturers quarters, classroom blocks, Senate building, student hostels almost completed. Construction of a teaching hospital is also going at ICT University. There is also the Aeronautical University located not far from the Chuba Okadigbo airport. Government sources said that the National University Commission has accredited the University to take off next academic session. The university will train engineers of various specialties. Indeed, a lot of structures are springing up at the massive sites in an effort to be ready for the take off of academic activities. From what is on ground, Nwifuru is investing a lot in the education sector and manpower development. He has awarded full Masters and PhD scholarship sponsorship to 1,400 Ebonyi indigenous students to universities in the United Kingdom and Nigeria; renovated some structures at State University and raised its subvention from N150 million to N280 million as well as released N700 outstanding subvention to the institutions. He also extended the good gesture to the State College of Education, Ikwo, which he upgraded to a University of Education. Many dilapidated primary and secondary schools have been rehabilitated. About 2000 primary and secondary school teachers were recruited. These are some of the governor’s major undertakings in the education sector. top.title: Harrison shocks Nunes on UFC return to retain title
top.description: Kayla Harrison has won 20 of her 21 professional fights [Getty Images] Kayla Harrison shocked returning great Amanda Nunes by submitting the former double champion to retain her bantamweight title at UFC 334 in New York. Nunes, 38, was fighting for the first time since she brought her glittering career to a close in 2023, after dominating at bantamweight and featherweight for years. Enticed by the challenge of fighting Harrison, the Brazilian came out of retirement for the bout but could not topple her friend and former training partner. Just 10 months after neck and spinal surgery, 36-year-old American Harrison ended the contest in the fourth round at Madison Square Garden with a rear-naked choke. Afterwards, Harrison reflected on the challenges she's overcome during her career. As a youngster, Harrison was sexually abused by her judo coach, who was sentenced to 10 years in prison after being found guilty. Harrison went on to become a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo before moving into mixed martial arts where she became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion and then won UFC bantamweight gold in just her third fight in the organisation. "I was sexually abused at a young age, statistically I'm not supposed to be here," said Harrison. "If you'd told me at six years old this would be my life and at 16, I wouldn't have believed you. "I'm really grateful, humbled and it's an honour and privilege to stand before you." In the main event, heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Josh Hokit. In a gruelling contest which featured a record 383 significant strikes in a UFC heavyweight bout, Frenchman Gane's counter striking off the back foot proved the difference. Harrison cements status as all-time great Harrison submitted Nunes with a rear-naked choke [Getty Images] Nunes left the UFC in 2023 as the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko, but it was the prospect of fighting Harrison which brought her out of retirement. The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, which Nunes left in 2022. Nunes started well and stung Harrison with a number of straight rights, but found herself in trouble at the end of the round with the American in a dominant position on the ground. Despite appearing to have an advantage on the feet, Nunes continued to try and grapple but it was a tactic which played into Harrison's hands. Harrison took the fight to the floor with a powerful hip toss, before later cutting Nunes with a big elbow and right hand on the ground. The decisive moment came in the fourth round as Harrison caught a kick before throwing Nunes off-balance and locking in the fight-ending submission. top.title: Rice hits back at Baena's claims that Yamal deserved Ballon d'Or over Kane
top.description: Rice hits back at Baena's claims that Yamal deserved Ballon d'Or over Kane Ahead of Spain's meeting with England, Declan Rice has hit back at Alex Baena's suggestion that Lamine Yamal deserved the Ballon d'Or over Harry Kane. When asked if the game is a great opportunity for Kane to show the world that he was the one who truly deserved that award, Rice believes the Bayern Munich star can do exactly that. “I think in Harry's case, for me and for everyone in England, Harry deserved the Ballon d'Or," the English midfielder said during the Three Lions' press conference. "I think if you look at his season, his numbers, the trophies he won and the way he performed in those games, it wasn't just about goals. "He delivered man-of-the-match performances. He was relentless. So, I can understand why every Spanish player is obviously going to say Lamine. "Lamine is an incredible player, one of the best players in the world, and he's going to win plenty of Ballon d'Or's in the future. “But I think this time it was right that Harry won, and I think he fully deserved it,” Rice concluded ahead of their meeting with the 2026 World Cup winners in Madrid.

top.title: Meet 2 African countries to ever break into top five FIFA World Ranking
top.description: Only two African countries have ever reached the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking, with Nigeria and Morocco achieving the historic feat more than three decades apart. The Super Eagles of Nigeria were the first African team to break into the world’s top five, reaching fifth place in April 1994. The achievement came during one of the most memorable periods in Nigerian football history, following the country’s victory at the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations in Tunisia. Nigeria, coached by Clemens Westerhof, had a talented generation featuring Rashidi Yekini, Daniel Amokachi, Emmanuel Amunike, Finidi George, Sunday Oliseh and Austin Jay-Jay Okocha. The Super Eagles also made their debut at the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, where they topped their group before being eliminated by Italy in the round of 16. For 32 years, Nigeria’s fifth-place ranking remained the highest position ever achieved by an African national team. However, Morocco joined the exclusive list in September 2026 after climbing to fifth in the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. The Atlas Lions’ rise followed a period of impressive performances, including their historic run to the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Morocco had also made history at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, becoming the first African country to reach the semi-finals of the competition. Their latest achievement saw them equal Nigeria’s record, making them the second African country to reach fifth place in the global ranking. According to FIFA, Morocco’s achievement matched the highest position ever attained by an African national team, a record Nigeria had held since April 1994. The two African countries are: Nigeria: Fifth place in April 1994. Morocco: Fifth place in September 2026. The two countries have therefore written their names into African football history, becoming the only representatives of the continent to reach the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. top.title: Key Stats that defined Penn State’s blowout victory over Minnesota
top.description: Penn State head coach Matt Campbell has done an excellent job of getting his team back on track. The blue and white were on a brutal four-game losing streak that took the air out of the season, but Campbell has responded with an impressive three-game winning streak. The defense has been excellent this entire year, with the exception of a couple of games in early October against Northwestern and USC , and now the offense is finally catching up to them. They had another good performance on Saturday against Minnesota, marking the first time since conference play began that the offense put together back-to-back solid showings. Let’s look at a few stats on both sides of the ball that show how Penn State pulled off this dominant 42-14 win . Rushing yards Running back Carson Hansen had the best game of his Penn State career last week against Washington . Well, he immediately outdid himself this week against Minnesota , going for 126 yards and a touchdown. The most impressive part of Hansen’s day is he got all of his production in the first half. He came up hobbled at the end of the second quarter and never returned, so hopefully it was just a precautionary measure since the team was winning 21-0 when he exited. Third-down conversions The Nittany Lions went into Saturday’s game as one of the best third-down defenses in the entire nation, and they certainly lived up to the billing. Minnesota was just 3-for-13 on third downs, and it was even wors in the first half when the offense was 1-for-7. The futility on money downs made it impossible for the offense to gain a rhythm. The unit was disjointed and inefficient the entire night, and it was largely because of Penn State’s exceptionality on third down. Drives starting in opponent’s territory This is a fairly unconventional stat, but it was one of the biggest reasons for the blue and white’s dominant win. They had three drives start in Minnesota’s territory, and they scored touchdowns on each of them. Conversely, the Golden Gophers never started a drive on Penn State’s end of the field. The Nittany Lions just continue to find unique advantages to win games. They possessed the ball for nearly 75% of game time against Purdue, and this week they had uncommonly favorable field position. You know what they say — good teams find ways to win games. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . top.title: Former Lyon and Napoli manager Rudi Garcia admits he came close to landing Manchester United job five years before Mauricio Pochettino's arrival
top.description: FBL-WC-2026-MATCH98-ESP-BEL - AFP Former Lyon and Napoli head coach Rudi Garcia has revealed he held two separate interviews for the Manchester United managerial post back in 2021. The Frenchman was considered for the Old Trafford hotseat five years prior to the club's latest appointment of Mauricio Pochettino. Frenchman recalls interim dugout shortlist Garcia emerged as a candidate to replace Ole Gunnar Solskjaer when the Norwegian's three-year reign ended following a heavy 4-1 Premier League defeat at Watford. Because that dismissal occurred midway through the 2021-22 campaign, the Red Devils hierarchy decided to bring in a temporary boss until the summer. The 62-year-old was available having left Lyon at the end of the previous season following nearly two years in charge. Two interviews precede Rangnick appointment Having previously won a Ligue 1 and Coupe de France double with Lille in 2011, the experienced tactician believed he had a strong case to take the reins in England. However, Old Trafford chiefs ultimately overlooked him and appointed Rangnick on a short-term contract in December 2021. Recalling how close he came to landing the role, Garcia told The Athletic : "Yes, I interviewed twice to work in this fantastic club, one of the best clubs in the world. "I'd like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough. It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over. I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf." Four permanent bosses follow departure Rangnick went on to oversee a sixth-place top-flight finish during his brief spell before Erik ten Hag arrived in the summer of 2022 as the first of four permanent appointments in just over four years. The Dutchman was eventually succeeded by Ruben Amorim in November 2024, prior to former midfielder Michael Carrick taking charge earlier this year . Following Carrick's sacking on Thursday, the club have now turned to former Tottenham Hotspur manager Pochettino to steady the ship. The Argentine will officially begin work this coming Thursday having penned a contract that runs until the summer of 2029. Mixed spells define subsequent career Meanwhile, Garcia returned to management with Al-Nassr, where he signed Cristiano Ronaldo following the forward's Old Trafford exit before being dismissed in April 2023 less than a season into his reign. He took over at Napoli three months later only to be sacked 12 games into the 2023-24 Serie A campaign. Most recently, he guided Belgium to this summer's World Cup quarter-finals before departing once eventual champions Spain eliminated them.

top.title: Surya blazes back in style, 21-ball 60 powers Mumbai to emphatic win over Hyderabad
top.description: Suryakumar Yadav could hardly have scripted a better response after what he recently described as a couple of "difficult months" following his omission from the Indian team despite captaining the country to the 2026 T20 World Cup title. Leading Mumbai in their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy opener against Hyderabad at Kolkata's Jadavpur University Ground on Saturday, the former India T20 skipper smashed an unbeaten 60 off just 21 balls, bringing up his half-century in a mere 15 deliveries. The 36-year-old hammered six fours and five sixes at a strike rate of 285.71 as Mumbai chased down 173 in just 13.1 overs, winning by seven wickets with 41 balls to spare. Batting at No. 4, Suryakumar tore into the Hyderabad attack from the outset and shared a 65-run stand off only 23 balls with Musheer Khan, who blasted 51 off 24 balls. Sooryavanshi disappoints on captaincy debut Teen batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi added another chapter to his remarkable rise by becoming the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history. At 15 years and 232 days, the Bihar prodigy surpassed Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who captained his national side at 17 years and 311 days in 2025. The youngster, entrusted with Bihar's leadership for the opening phase of the tournament, endured a disappointing outing on the field. He made 18 off 12 balls as Bihar, who scored 137 for nine, went down to Saurashtra by five wickets. Mayank's 5 wkts help Delhi win Pacer Mayank Yadav ripped through Jammu & Kashmir with figures of five for 14 in three overs to power Delhi to a commanding 103-run victory in Indore. Delhi piled up 243 for six, powered by Himmat Singh's 63 off 26 balls and Priyansh Arya's 58 off 29, before Mayank's pace proved too hot to handle. top.title: Barcelona receive €100 million offer for La Masia star amid Chelsea, Manchester United interest
top.description: Barcelona receive €100 million offer for La Masia star amid Chelsea, Manchester United interest Even in a season where Lamine Yamal and Raphinha have attracted the limelight once again through their exceptional performances, Fermin Lopez has proven why he is such an important part of Barcelona. The Spanish international has quietly emerged as one of Barcelona’s most productive players with eight goals and seven assists in all competitions. Fermin’s brilliant season has not gone unnoticed either, with a number of Premier League clubs keen on signing the playmaker. Barcelona receive €100 million offer for Fermin Fermin has transformed into a genuine star at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) According to Diario SPORT , a host of Premier League clubs who were keen on Fermin last summer have revisited their interest in the player. In fact, Barcelona have even received an offer of around €100 million for the services of the Spanish international. Chelsea, in particular, had tabled a bid of around €70 million last summer. But it is likely that the Blues, along with other Premier League clubs such as Manchester United have tabled a bid higher than that. Chelsea and Man United are apparently the teams who have shown the most concrete interest in signing Fermin. Fermin has no desire to leave Fermin Lopez wants to remain at Barcelona. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) However, Barcelona are not worried about the prospect of Fermin Lopez leaving the club anytime shown. The player has shown no desire to leave Barcelona, even though he is a distant third behind Yamal and Raphinha, as far as the team’s biggest attacking stars are concerned. Fermin has a contract at Camp Nou until 2031, which gives the Blaugrana significant leverage even when a Premier League team does make a push to sign the player. Barcelona are also aware of Fermin’s progress and are expected to soon sit down with the player’s representative over a new contract that will likely come with a significant raise in salary. In any case, Fermin has turned deaf ears to interest from these Premier League clubs and will not consider an exit from Barcelona, no matter how lucrative an offer he gets.

top.title: Peter Shilton reacts to Harry Kane becoming England’s most-capped player
top.description: Photo by Carl Recine - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Peter Shilton held the record for most caps by an England player in history, earning 125 between 1970 and 1990. Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane broke that record when he made his 126th appearance in Wembley Stadium against Croatia in the UEFA Nations League, and Shilton says Kane and only Kane deserved to break his record. “I’ve held the record for quite a few years now, but if anyone deserves to overtake me, it’s Harry,” Shilton said (via FIFA as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “I couldn’t think of anyone better. He’s been an incredible servant and leader for so long now, and has scored plenty of goals along the way. I think I will be going on to the pitch to present him with something.” Kane presented his Ballon d’Or before a magnificent tifo honoring his success prior to kickoff and earned his side the win by converting a penalty for a 2-1 win. Some big names left the club on loan and have endured mixed fortunes in the first few months of the new campaign. With domestic football currently on pause due to the international break, let’s take a look at how they have all been getting on. Ronald Araujo Uruguayan defender Ronald Araujo agreed a season-long loan with Liverpool and has been a huge hit in the Premier League with the Reds so far this season. The defender was in need of a fresh start after a tough time at Barcelona and has found his form, his smile and a whole lot of love in England at Anfield. Araujo has become a regular at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side and seems to be thriving on the Premier League’s physicality and intensity. The center-back has also scored twice and already has Liverpool fans asking the club to sign him up . There is reportedly a buy option in his loan deal, although Araujo has insisted it’s too early to talk about the future. What is certain is that the loan has been a great success so far for all concerned. There’s still a long way to go between now and the end of the campaign but Araujo looks rejuvenated in the red shirt of Liverpool. Marc Casado Marc Casado reluctantly left Barcelona in the summer, leaving it until the last minute to seal a temporary move to Deportivo in a bid for regular minutes. The arrival of Rodri in the summer saw Casado slip even further down the pecking order at Barcelona and he chose Deportivo after admitting he was impressed by the club on a previous visit with the Catalans. Unfortunately for Casado, all has not gone smoothly so far. The midfielder made four appearances and was then sidelined with a fractured collarbone that required surgery. The Barcelona loanee was expected to miss three months but managed to return at the start of November against Espanyol. Now fully fit, he will be hoping to make an impact after an injury-interrupted start to life in A Coruna. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Last night (Sat., Nov. 14, 2026), Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) ventured forth to Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York for UFC 334 . Twin title fights topped the promotion’s return to MSG, making for an exciting and high-profile night of action. In the main event, Ciryl Gane aimed for the first defense of his newly-minted Heavyweight crown opposite divisional upstart Josh Hokit . In addition, Amanda Nunes returned after nearly three years on the sidelines in an attempt to recapture her Bantamweight crown from Judo Olympian Kayla Harrison . The rest of the card was stacked with fun matchups and interesting talent, so let’s get right to the best performances and highlight finishes of the evening: A Record-Setting Heavyweight War Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit was an outstanding scrap, the best Heavyweight fight in quite some time. Gane started strong. Hokit wrestled right away and surged forward relentlessly, forcing Gane onto the back foot immediately. From his bike, Gane was nevertheless able to snap Hokit’s chin back repeatedly. It didn’t deter Hokit and his fastball of a right hand, but those jabs were the most significant punches of the opening frame. In addition, Gane did well to start punching the body early in the fight. Gane was operating without kicks, however, in fear of the takedown, and he was sprinting all over the cage. As a result, he started breathing more heavily in the second, and Hokit was able to close the gap more often. By the third, Hokit was dictating the pace and landing the better shots. Not only did he connect with the right hand, but he started stomping on Gane’s foot like he was trying to put out a fire, and he also scored some knifing elbows from the clinch. In round four, Gane made a decision that changed the entire fight. After running around for 15 straight minutes, Gane began to stand his ground and put more weight into his strikes. In addition, Gane had avoided throwing kicks and knees for much of the fight in fear of the takedown. Since Hokit hadn’t managed to do much with his wrestling in the first three rounds, Gane was able to more effectively open up with his other weapons and take that risk. A ripping left kick to the body opened the fourth, and I would have loved to see more of them. Instead, Gane found his best success of the fight with hard knees to the body. Sitting down on his shots produced more clinches in the open, and Gane used those clinches to frame and create distance for knees to the mid-section. Hokit may have kept his poker face through all those jabs early, but he couldn’t hide his reaction to the knees. top.title: “Jessica Pegula Did Mirra Andreeva A Favor” – Serena Williams’ Coach Explains How WTA Finals Controversy Became A ‘Catalyst’ For Teenager
top.description: Mirra Andreeva © Imagn Serena Williams’ coach Rennae Stubbs believes Mirra Andreeva’s remarkable run at the 2026 WTA Finals stems from controversial comments Jessica Pegula made about her ahead of the year-end championships. Andreeva, making her WTA Finals debut this year, has reached the final after three dominant Round Robin phase wins. The 19-year-old then defeated Pegula in another impressive semifinal. During a practice session in the tournament buildup that was streamed live, a courtside microphone picked up Pegula brazenly criticizing Andreeva’s mentality. The American veteran called the young Russian a ‘diva’ and said that if Andreeva improves her attitude, she will go on to achieve even greater things. Andreeva, despite her tender age, already has six senior singles titles, including this year’s Roland Garros crown. After the 19-year-old’s 6-3, 6-4 win over Pegula in the semis, Stubbs took to X and wrote: “I think @JPegula did Mirra a favor by making those comments last week. It was a wake up call by a peer & it may have just been the catalyst to make her the best player in the world!! 😂 … because she has been very Un-diva like this week! Head down, great attitude & crushing!!” Mirra Andreeva’s victory over Jessica Pegula at WTA Finals 2026 ensures World No. 2 spot for the youngster Andreeva will replace Aryna Sabalenka as the new World No. 2 once the new rankings are published after the WTA Finals conclude. Interestingly, in the Round Robin phase, Andreeva and Sabalenka had locked horns, and the youngster came away with a deserving 6-4, 6-0 win over the former No. 1. Elina Svitolina of Ukraine awaits Andreeva in the final , and the 19-year-old should be confident going into the match. The youngster clashed with the veteran and former WTA Finals champion in their opening Round Robin match. Andreeva won by the same score she recorded against Sabalenka. Andreeva is also the youngest player since the iconic Maria Sharapova to reach the WTA Finals’ championship match. In 2004, Sharapova not only reached the last hurdle, but also conquered it by defeating the legendary Serena Williams in three sets. top.description: The UFC 334 main event delivered a much-needed boost to the heavyweight division. Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit went to war for five rounds in an all-out slugfest, with the champion ultimately retaining his title via unanimous decision. Much of the pre-fight discussion revolved around the controversy surrounding Gane being elevated to heavyweight champion and whether Hokit deserved a title shot in the first place. nigeria.title: Nwifuru is silently taking Ebonyi to greater heights, and touching every sector
nigeria.description: By Anayo Okoli The trending is narrative given to the public in and outside Ebonyi State by opposition is that Governor Francis Nwifuru is not working. And this narrative has gained currency among the people. But a visit to the state indicates that indeed the contrary is the case. The Governor is indeed doing working and touching every sector of development. The reality on ground is that a lot of development is happening in the State. Across the 13 local government areas of thespian state, no community is left out, at least with a road project. According to records, on assumption of office, Governor Francis Nwifuru unfolded what he called “People’s Charter of Needs” as a priority guide to his development trajectory and his administration has followed this religiously. In fact some of the ongoing projects are landmark projects that would project the state to national and even international maps. For instance, two specialized universities being built by the government will change the education landscape of the State. One of them, the ICT University has taken off at a temporary site with over 100 students receiving education free of charge. Work at the permanent site in Oferekpe, located in a vast land space, is ongoing with many sections, including lecturers quarters, classroom blocks, Senate building, student hostels almost completed. Construction of a teaching hospital is also going at ICT University. There is also the Aeronautical University located not far from the Chuba Okadigbo airport. Government sources said that the National University Commission has accredited the University to take off next academic session. The university will train engineers of various specialties. Indeed, a lot of structures are springing up at the massive sites in an effort to be ready for the take off of academic activities. From what is on ground, Nwifuru is investing a lot in the education sector and manpower development. He has awarded full Masters and PhD scholarship sponsorship to 1,400 Ebonyi indigenous students to universities in the United Kingdom and Nigeria; renovated some structures at State University and raised its subvention from N150 million to N280 million as well as released N700 outstanding subvention to the institutions. He also extended the good gesture to the State College of Education, Ikwo, which he upgraded to a University of Education. Many dilapidated primary and secondary schools have been rehabilitated. About 2000 primary and secondary school teachers were recruited. These are some of the governor’s major undertakings in the education sector. nigeria.title: Meet 2 African countries to ever break into top five FIFA World Ranking
nigeria.description: Only two African countries have ever reached the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking, with Nigeria and Morocco achieving the historic feat more than three decades apart. The Super Eagles of Nigeria were the first African team to break into the world’s top five, reaching fifth place in April 1994. The achievement came during one of the most memorable periods in Nigerian football history, following the country’s victory at the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations in Tunisia. Nigeria, coached by Clemens Westerhof, had a talented generation featuring Rashidi Yekini, Daniel Amokachi, Emmanuel Amunike, Finidi George, Sunday Oliseh and Austin Jay-Jay Okocha. The Super Eagles also made their debut at the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, where they topped their group before being eliminated by Italy in the round of 16. For 32 years, Nigeria’s fifth-place ranking remained the highest position ever achieved by an African national team. However, Morocco joined the exclusive list in September 2026 after climbing to fifth in the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. The Atlas Lions’ rise followed a period of impressive performances, including their historic run to the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Morocco had also made history at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, becoming the first African country to reach the semi-finals of the competition. Their latest achievement saw them equal Nigeria’s record, making them the second African country to reach fifth place in the global ranking. According to FIFA, Morocco’s achievement matched the highest position ever attained by an African national team, a record Nigeria had held since April 1994. The two African countries are: Nigeria: Fifth place in April 1994. Morocco: Fifth place in September 2026. The two countries have therefore written their names into African football history, becoming the only representatives of the continent to reach the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. nigeria.title: Mbappe available for clash with Turkey – Zidane
nigeria.description: Kylian Mbappe is available to play in France’s final Nations League group fixture against Turkey, coach Zinedine Zidane said on Saturday, as Les Bleus seek a spot in the quarter-finals. Real Madrid forward Mbappe missed Thursday’s defeat to Group A1 leaders Italy with a hamstring problem, but Zidane confirmed: “He will be with us tomorrow (Sunday). Mbappe, who has netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season, was back in the France squad for this international break after missing his country’s previous three matches through injury. Zidane said Mbappe’s return “changes everything”, adding: “I’d rather have him with us than not.” The 54-year-old, a World Cup winner with France in 1998 and European champion two years later, denied any tensions with Mbappe and said his relationship with his star striker was going “perfectly”. “I can’t stop people saying what they’re saying, but it’s nonsense and quite irritating,” said Zidane. France are second in Group A1, level on 10 points with Italy, and need just a draw against Turkey in Bordeaux to secure qualification for the Nations League quarter-finals. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s mission in S/Africa urges calm in row over Ramaphosa spokesman’s remarks
nigeria.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has urged restraint and reconciliation after remarks by President Cyril Ramaphosa’s spokesman, Vincent Magwenya, about Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Mr Femi Fani-Kayode. The Mission said on its verified X handle that it wants cordial relations between both countries preserved. The row followed a disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream when Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa in Tshwane. The broadcast was restored while Ramaphosa was addressing the ambassadors. Magwenya had then accused Fani-Kayode of of lying about Ramaphosa intervening in the controversy surrounding his diplomatic credentials. The Mission said Fani-Kayode, one of the last diplomats to present credentials, complained that his speech had been deliberately omitted. It said he raised the matter with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him all was well. It said the disagreement should have been handled through diplomatic channels and urged Magwenya to show restraint. The Mission described Magwenya’s conduct as provocative and diplomatically inappropriate. It said its post was meant to reject what it called his attempt to portray Fani-Kayode as dishonest and to damage Nigeria’s image. “To us this matter is closed, but if you wish to escalate it you are welcome to do so and we are up to the task. A word is enough for the wise,” the Mission said. It commended Ramaphosa for intervening. “Thankfully your President had the decency and presence of mind to put out the fire and direct you and your state broadcaster to do the right thing. He literally saved the day,” it said. The post Nigeria’s mission in S/Africa urges calm in row over Ramaphosa spokesman’s remarks appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire The Ohworode of Olomu, HRM Albert Akpomudje, SAN, FCIArb, Eyavwien-Alaka I, is marking his first year coronation anniversary. In this interview, Akpomuje bares his mind on his experience as a traditional ruler, Chairman, Body of Benchers and a practising lawyer. Excerpts: Your Majesty, it’s been one year since you ascended the throne. What has been your experience as the traditional ruler of ancient Olomu Kingdom? Well, I must say it’s been a very exciting one year. First of all, I must commend my subjects on the fact that since after the coronation on the 15th of November, 2025, they have been very, very loyal. After the coronation I decided to go round the 15 communities under Olomu Kingdom, and the excitement of the people during the time gave me a very positive and commendable impression of the people; it was like they were seeing their king for the first time visiting their communities, which had not happened before. They did everything to make the occasion memorable. That encouraged me to say I have loyal subjects in Olomu Kingdom. How have you been coping with your legal practice and also continuing your role as the Chairman of Body of Benchers? Well, it’s not been easy. But I want to thank God who has given me the strength and good health to be able to manage three things or four together. One, I still go to my office to do what I’m used to. What I don’t do frequently now is maybe going to court, but I’m on ground. I’m still in charge of the office, and I have very able juniors. Then, of course, the Body of Benchers, I have to be on ground in Abuja for meetings and so many other things and then you have to come back to the traditional set up. But I want to thank God that I’ve been coping well. It is exciting. I know that it is not too easy. And the reason why I’m enjoying it is that I’m having cooperation from my people. So far, there are no issues. I don’t have issues with them. They rely on me. nigeria.title: CHINA DIARIES: The Future of farming
nigeria.description: When we talk about China’s development, the images that often come to mind are high-speed trains, towering skyscrapers, electric vehicles and impressive infrastructure. But there is another quiet revolution taking place, one that is just as important to China’s future: agriculture. I had an opportunity to explore this during a visit to Yangling, in Shaanxi Province, a place that has become an important centre for agricultural science, research, innovation and technology. Our visit took us to three facilities: the SCO Demonstration Base for Agricultural Technology Exchange and Training, the Yangling Smart Agriculture Demonstration Park, and Yangling Liangke Agricultural Science and Technology Co. Ltd. What I saw offered an interesting glimpse into how China is using science and technology to rethink farming, improve productivity and strengthen food security. China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria! 2027: We’ll fight Tinubu in South, North-Central, sweep North-West, North-East – Amaechi And, naturally, it got me thinking about Nigeria. Where farming meets the digital age One of the most interesting parts of the visit was seeing how technology is being integrated into everyday agricultural activities. At the smart agriculture demonstration facility, I saw a control station where plants are monitored through screens. Rather than relying entirely on physical observation, information about growing conditions can be monitored centrally, allowing operators to keep track of what is happening inside the growing facilities. It was a reminder that modern farming is increasingly becoming a data-driven activity. The farmer of the future may still walk through the farm, inspect the crops and get his hands dirty, but technology is giving him additional tools to make better decisions. I also saw vegetables being cultivated indoors in a controlled environment. It was fascinating to see food production taking place in a setting that looked quite different from the conventional farms we are familiar with in Nigeria. The idea is to manage growing conditions and create a more controlled environment for production. Such systems can help reduce dependence on some external weather conditions and make production more predictable, although their commercial viability depends on energy, infrastructure and operating costs. Another interesting sight was the display of grains and seedlings. These may look ordinary at first glance, but they represent an important part of the agricultural value chain: research, seed development and the effort to improve the quality and productivity of crops before they even get to the farm. nigeria.description: …LASEMA responds to three emergencies across Lagos, rescues stranded motorists By Matthew Johnson A woman has been killed after a Lexus car rammed into a commercial minibus at Igando, Lagos State, in an accident that also left the bus driver injured. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) disclosed this while reporting its response to three separate emergencies across the state. The fatal accident occurred in the early hours of Friday, November 13, 2026, around Ajay Hotel, Igando, involving a Lexus car, a commercial minibus popularly known as Korope, and a pedestrian. According to preliminary information released by LASEMA, the Lexus car, which was reportedly fleeing, rammed into the minibus with registration number SMK 514 YG, causing the vehicle to strike the woman. The woman died in the incident, while the minibus driver sustained injuries and was taken to hospital before the arrival of the agency’s response team. Her remains were subsequently handed over to her relatives by officers of the Nigeria Police Force, Igando Division, in accordance with established procedures. LASEMA said its Dolphin Team, stationed in Igando, was immediately deployed after receiving a distress call and arrived at the scene within minutes. The agency, working alongside the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and the police, secured the accident scene, managed traffic and coordinated the removal of the affected vehicle. The minibus was recovered and towed to the Igando Police Station with the assistance of a private tow truck, while normal traffic flow was restored. In a statement signed by LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, the state government expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured driver a speedy recovery. Oke-Osanyintolu also disclosed that the agency attended to two other emergencies within the same operational period. At Ketu-Epe Road, LASEMA concluded its follow-up response to an earlier accident involving a white minibus that plunged into a ditch. Police officers at the scene confirmed that the driver and three passengers were receiving treatment at Ketu General Hospital. The permanent secretary said the vehicle was not obstructing traffic and that the incident had been formally handed over to the police at Ketu Division for further action. In another operation, LASEMA’s Lion Squad responded to a broken-down trailer conveying a 40-foot container along Imota Road, inward Ikorodu, around Agbowa. nigeria.title: Kano drug war: PCN denies shielding illicit drug dealers
nigeria.description: …says 1,631 drug outlets sealed in 2026, challenges task force chairman to provide evidence of alleged staff involvement By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) has denied allegations that it is shielding illicit drug dealers and facilitating the distribution of controlled substances in Kano State, insisting that it remains committed to enforcing pharmaceutical regulations. The council described the allegations by the Chairman of the Kano State Multi-Agency Taskforce on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, Muhuyi Magaji Rimin-Gado, as baseless and misleading, challenging him to provide verifiable evidence to substantiate his claims. In a rebuttal issued on Saturday and signed by Pharm. Hasiya Ladan, Consultant Pharmacist at the PCN Kano State Office, on behalf of the Registrar and Chief Executive Officer, the council disclosed that it sealed 1,631 pharmaceutical premises in Kano State in 2026 following inspections of 2,304 drug outlets. It also said 15 investigations into suspected regulatory violations were ongoing in the state, while its national enforcement team had visited Kano twice this year, in April and September. The rebuttal followed allegations made by Rimin-Gado at a press conference in Kano on November 14, where he accused the PCN and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) of allegedly protecting drug dealers operating in the state. The task force chairman had, among other things, questioned the circumstances surrounding the issuance of import licences to pharmaceutical companies dealing in pregabalin, particularly after NAFDAC rescheduled the drug as a controlled substance on September 14, 2026. He also accused the PCN of registering a pharmaceutical outlet at No. 10 Apple Avenue, allegedly located in a residential area, which he claimed was being used as a concealed distribution point for the drug. Rimin-Gado further alleged that some PCN officials were involved in clandestine drug businesses and questioned the council’s capacity to effectively regulate pharmaceutical activities in Kano, citing its relatively small number of personnel in the state. However, the PCN maintained that the regulation of pharmaceutical premises was a statutory federal responsibility backed by the Constitution, legislation and judicial pronouncements. It cited Item 21 of Part I of the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, arguing that drugs and poisons fall under the Exclusive Legislative List and that their regulation is therefore the responsibility of the Federal Government through authorised agencies. The council also referenced the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Act 2022, the Supreme Court judgment in Pharmacists Board of Nigeria v. Franklin Adegbesote (1986), and a February 16, 2024 judgment of the Federal High Court, Kano, as legal authorities affirming its regulatory mandate. nigeria.description: …404 ‘arrested’ in 20 months By Nnamdi Ojiego The image of an elderly grandmother or grandfather being led away by anti-narcotics officers over alleged involvement in drug trafficking is one that challenges conventional perceptions of who participates in the illicit drug trade. Yet, a succession of arrests involving people in their 60s, 70s and even older has brought an uncomfortable question to the fore: Why are people who should ordinarily be enjoying their retirement years becoming involved in the dangerous business of transporting, storing and distributing illicit drugs? In Nigeria, the figures supplied by Femi Babafemi, spokesperson of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) suggest that the phenomenon deserves closer attention. The agency arrested 240 persons aged 60 and above for drug-related offences in 2025, comprising 191 men and 49 women. Between January and August 2026, another 164 elderly suspects, including 128 men and 36 women, were arrested. The figures bring the total number of elderly persons arrested within the 20-month period to 404. Men accounted for the overwhelming majority, representing approximately 80 per cent of the arrests in 2025 and 78 per cent in the first eight months of 2026. Calculated strategy Although the 2026 figures cover only eight months and cannot be directly compared with the full-year 2025 total, the number of arrests already recorded points to the continued involvement of older people in drug-related activities. It also raises questions about the circumstances drawing them into a trade whose consequences include lengthy imprisonment, financial ruin, damaged family relationships and, in some cases, serious health risks. The NDLEA also reported seizing 6,998.77 kilogrammes of illicit drugs in connection with elderly suspects in 2025, compared with 1,479.988 kilogrammes between January and August 2026. From couriers to local dealers The cases recorded by the NDLEA in 2026 provide a glimpse into the different ways older people are becoming involved in the illicit drug trade. On March 14, 2026, NDLEA operatives arrested 74-year-old Ikwuakalom Nwakoro Emeka at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, while he was preparing to board a British Airways flight to London. The agency alleged that 11 kilogrammes of cocaine were discovered in his luggage, concealed in food items, including ground dry pepper. He reportedly told investigators he was travelling to Britain on holiday. Barely three months later, another high-profile case emerged at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos. On June 28, operatives arrested 67-year-old Mary Yetunde Barek, a Nigerian-British woman who worked as a caregiver in the United Kingdom, while she was preparing to board a Virgin Atlantic flight to London. nigeria.description: …Report says 640 killed in October as a result of broader insecurity …Experts warn against violence, fake news By Nnamdi Ojiego 60 days to the 2027 general elections, concerns are mounting over the safety of the electoral process as rising insecurity, attacks on political gatherings and the spread of misinformation threaten to undermine citizens’ participation in the polls. The concerns have been heightened by fresh incidents of political violence in different parts of the country, including Calabar, Cross River State, Asaba, Delta State, and Sokoto, where political supporters and opposition figures have reportedly come under attack. The developments have renewed questions about the preparedness of security agencies to protect candidates, party supporters and voters, particularly in a country already grappling with banditry, insurgency, kidnapping and communal violence. A report by the Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD), Nigeria Election Security Tracker for October 2026 provides a troubling picture of the security situation. It recorded 640 deaths during the month (October), representing a 61.62 per cent increase from the 396 deaths recorded in September. Of the 640 deaths, 638 were attributed to broader insecurity, while two resulted from election-related attacks in Enugu and Ebonyi. The North-East accounted for the highest number of fatalities, with 409 deaths. The report also documented 16 election-related incidents in October, compared with 14 in September, representing a 14.29 per cent increase. Attacks on campaign gatherings and convoys accounted for 11 of the 16 incidents. Other cases involved assaults on individuals, attacks on political property and the restriction of a political gathering. The incidents affected several political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC) and African Democratic Congress (ADC), which each recorded four cases, while the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) recorded three. Two of the incidents were fatal. Ifeanyi Nwolie died from gunshot injuries sustained during the NDC campaign launch in Enugu on October 10. In Ebonyi, gunmen attacked the convoy of NDC candidate, Rollins Offia-Nwali, on October 22, killing one person, injuring three others and burning his vehicle. The candidate reportedly escaped. The CDD report also documented attacks on ADC convoys in Igueben and Kogi, disruption of PDP consultations in Calabar, an attack on an ADC candidate’s meeting in Obosi, Anambra State, and the prevention of supporters from gathering for the Obi-Kwankwaso march in Abuja. Although broader insecurity accounted for most of the fatalities, the report warned that its consequences could extend to the electoral process, particularly in communities where residents have been displaced or roads have become unsafe. nigeria.title: Christian persecution in Nigeria worrisome — Catholic bishops
nigeria.description: By Chidi Nkwopara Church leaders have expressed concern over the increasing cases of violent persecution of Christians in parts of Nigeria, saying the disturbing trend has worsened over the past two decades. The Apostolic Nuncio to Nigeria, Archbishop Michael Francis Crotty, and the Archbishop of Owerri, Most Rev. Lucius Iwejuru Ugorji, raised the concern at the weekend in Owerri during their respective addresses at the 18th National Conference of the Association of Papal Knights and Medalists in Nigeria (APKMN). In his address, Crotty said Christians had suffered persecution in different forms throughout Nigeria’s history, but noted that violent forms of persecution had become more pronounced in the last two decades. “In the history of Nigeria, Christians have suffered persecution in different forms, and this disturbing phenomenon has increased within the last two decades, especially the violent forms of persecution. “In recent years, Christians have been targeted by kidnappers, and many lay faithful and priests have been kidnapped. “Many of those kidnapped were killed, and others were released after ransoms were paid. Thousands of churches have been attacked and destroyed since the beginning of Boko Haram and the activities of herdsmen in more recent years,” he said. The Apostolic Nuncio also alleged that Christians in some parts of the country, particularly the North and North-Central regions, had been denied legitimate access to land for the construction of places of worship. “Very often the issue of persecution of Christians in Nigeria is politicised and approached with some sort of bias and religious sentiments. “There is no doubt that people of other faiths have also been affected by insecurity in Nigeria. However, we cannot deny the fact that Christians have been specifically targeted in some parts of the country. “Our concern should be the necessary actions to take in order to bring the unnecessary killing of all citizens to an end, whether they are Christian or of other faiths,” he said. He described the conference theme, “Strategic Engagements in Addressing Christian Persecution in Nigeria: Toward Coordinated Response”, as timely, stressing the need for collective action across religious and community lines. In his address, Archbishop Ugorji said the human and material consequences of the country’s insecurity remained alarming, irrespective of whether the crisis was viewed as targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict. “Ultimately, whether the crisis is perceived as a targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict, the human and material toll is undeniable. “It is deeply troubling that tens of thousands have lost their lives, millions remain internally displaced, the education of thousands of children is truncated, and millions of naira have been lost through destruction of property and paying ransom,” he said. nigeria.title: Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has said the state already has the structure for state police to commence and for that reason, the state House of Assembly was one of the first to pass the law as recommended by the National Assembly. Okpebholo spoke in an interview with journalists in Benin-City as part of activities to mark his second year anniversary. “We are prepared. We were one of the first to sign into law, when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo state is safe.” He said his state already has a working security architecture it has tested that could be used to track criminals even outside the state,” he said. Okpebholo said “Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days and as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. So somebody has to be prudent with everything.” On security in the state, Governor Okpebholo said his administration took stiff measures to reduce the level of killings and kidnapping in the state. Some of the measures, he said, was destroying any building that was linked to kidnapping and cult related activities in the state irrespective of the social status of the person involved. He said: “These are stiff measures we have taken that are really working for us. To be honest with you, if not that we have done that, maybe you won’t be able to stay in Benin for two nights. Today nightlife is back, business is booming at night, even supermarkets are beginning to open at night. “In the next few weeks, it will be safer because there will be police at every corner of the state to watch everyone. They will be equipped even with motorbikes so that when somebody thinks he can run, then they will follow the person. Whether you take a bush path, they will follow you up.” The post Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. sports.title: Harrison shocks Nunes on UFC return to retain title
sports.description: Kayla Harrison has won 20 of her 21 professional fights [Getty Images] Kayla Harrison shocked returning great Amanda Nunes by submitting the former double champion to retain her bantamweight title at UFC 334 in New York. Nunes, 38, was fighting for the first time since she brought her glittering career to a close in 2023, after dominating at bantamweight and featherweight for years. Enticed by the challenge of fighting Harrison, the Brazilian came out of retirement for the bout but could not topple her friend and former training partner. Just 10 months after neck and spinal surgery, 36-year-old American Harrison ended the contest in the fourth round at Madison Square Garden with a rear-naked choke. Afterwards, Harrison reflected on the challenges she's overcome during her career. As a youngster, Harrison was sexually abused by her judo coach, who was sentenced to 10 years in prison after being found guilty. Harrison went on to become a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo before moving into mixed martial arts where she became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion and then won UFC bantamweight gold in just her third fight in the organisation. "I was sexually abused at a young age, statistically I'm not supposed to be here," said Harrison. "If you'd told me at six years old this would be my life and at 16, I wouldn't have believed you. "I'm really grateful, humbled and it's an honour and privilege to stand before you." In the main event, heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Josh Hokit. In a gruelling contest which featured a record 383 significant strikes in a UFC heavyweight bout, Frenchman Gane's counter striking off the back foot proved the difference. Harrison cements status as all-time great Harrison submitted Nunes with a rear-naked choke [Getty Images] Nunes left the UFC in 2023 as the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. sports.title: Key Stats that defined Penn State’s blowout victory over Minnesota
sports.description: Penn State head coach Matt Campbell has done an excellent job of getting his team back on track. The blue and white were on a brutal four-game losing streak that took the air out of the season, but Campbell has responded with an impressive three-game winning streak. The defense has been excellent this entire year, with the exception of a couple of games in early October against Northwestern and USC , and now the offense is finally catching up to them. They had another good performance on Saturday against Minnesota, marking the first time since conference play began that the offense put together back-to-back solid showings. Let’s look at a few stats on both sides of the ball that show how Penn State pulled off this dominant 42-14 win . Rushing yards Running back Carson Hansen had the best game of his Penn State career last week against Washington . Well, he immediately outdid himself this week against Minnesota , going for 126 yards and a touchdown. The most impressive part of Hansen’s day is he got all of his production in the first half. He came up hobbled at the end of the second quarter and never returned, so hopefully it was just a precautionary measure since the team was winning 21-0 when he exited. Third-down conversions The Nittany Lions went into Saturday’s game as one of the best third-down defenses in the entire nation, and they certainly lived up to the billing. Minnesota was just 3-for-13 on third downs, and it was even wors in the first half when the offense was 1-for-7. The futility on money downs made it impossible for the offense to gain a rhythm. The unit was disjointed and inefficient the entire night, and it was largely because of Penn State’s exceptionality on third down. Drives starting in opponent’s territory This is a fairly unconventional stat, but it was one of the biggest reasons for the blue and white’s dominant win. They had three drives start in Minnesota’s territory, and they scored touchdowns on each of them. Conversely, the Golden Gophers never started a drive on Penn State’s end of the field. The Nittany Lions just continue to find unique advantages to win games. They possessed the ball for nearly 75% of game time against Purdue, and this week they had uncommonly favorable field position. sports.description: FBL-WC-2026-MATCH98-ESP-BEL - AFP Former Lyon and Napoli head coach Rudi Garcia has revealed he held two separate interviews for the Manchester United managerial post back in 2021. The Frenchman was considered for the Old Trafford hotseat five years prior to the club's latest appointment of Mauricio Pochettino. Frenchman recalls interim dugout shortlist Garcia emerged as a candidate to replace Ole Gunnar Solskjaer when the Norwegian's three-year reign ended following a heavy 4-1 Premier League defeat at Watford. Because that dismissal occurred midway through the 2021-22 campaign, the Red Devils hierarchy decided to bring in a temporary boss until the summer. The 62-year-old was available having left Lyon at the end of the previous season following nearly two years in charge. Two interviews precede Rangnick appointment Having previously won a Ligue 1 and Coupe de France double with Lille in 2011, the experienced tactician believed he had a strong case to take the reins in England. However, Old Trafford chiefs ultimately overlooked him and appointed Rangnick on a short-term contract in December 2021. Recalling how close he came to landing the role, Garcia told The Athletic : "Yes, I interviewed twice to work in this fantastic club, one of the best clubs in the world. "I'd like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough. It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over. I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf." Four permanent bosses follow departure Rangnick went on to oversee a sixth-place top-flight finish during his brief spell before Erik ten Hag arrived in the summer of 2022 as the first of four permanent appointments in just over four years. The Dutchman was eventually succeeded by Ruben Amorim in November 2024, prior to former midfielder Michael Carrick taking charge earlier this year . Following Carrick's sacking on Thursday, the club have now turned to former Tottenham Hotspur manager Pochettino to steady the ship. The Argentine will officially begin work this coming Thursday having penned a contract that runs until the summer of 2029. Mixed spells define subsequent career Meanwhile, Garcia returned to management with Al-Nassr, where he signed Cristiano Ronaldo following the forward's Old Trafford exit before being dismissed in April 2023 less than a season into his reign. He took over at Napoli three months later only to be sacked 12 games into the 2023-24 Serie A campaign. Most recently, he guided Belgium to this summer's World Cup quarter-finals before departing once eventual champions Spain eliminated them.

sports.title: Surya blazes back in style, 21-ball 60 powers Mumbai to emphatic win over Hyderabad
sports.description: Suryakumar Yadav could hardly have scripted a better response after what he recently described as a couple of "difficult months" following his omission from the Indian team despite captaining the country to the 2026 T20 World Cup title. Leading Mumbai in their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy opener against Hyderabad at Kolkata's Jadavpur University Ground on Saturday, the former India T20 skipper smashed an unbeaten 60 off just 21 balls, bringing up his half-century in a mere 15 deliveries. The 36-year-old hammered six fours and five sixes at a strike rate of 285.71 as Mumbai chased down 173 in just 13.1 overs, winning by seven wickets with 41 balls to spare. Batting at No. 4, Suryakumar tore into the Hyderabad attack from the outset and shared a 65-run stand off only 23 balls with Musheer Khan, who blasted 51 off 24 balls. Sooryavanshi disappoints on captaincy debut Teen batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi added another chapter to his remarkable rise by becoming the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history. At 15 years and 232 days, the Bihar prodigy surpassed Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who captained his national side at 17 years and 311 days in 2025. The youngster, entrusted with Bihar's leadership for the opening phase of the tournament, endured a disappointing outing on the field. He made 18 off 12 balls as Bihar, who scored 137 for nine, went down to Saurashtra by five wickets. Mayank's 5 wkts help Delhi win Pacer Mayank Yadav ripped through Jammu & Kashmir with figures of five for 14 in three overs to power Delhi to a commanding 103-run victory in Indore. Delhi piled up 243 for six, powered by Himmat Singh's 63 off 26 balls and Priyansh Arya's 58 off 29, before Mayank's pace proved too hot to handle. Karnataka prevail Pacers Abhilash Shetty (4-26) and Vijaykumar Vyshak (3-28) shared seven wickets as Karnataka restricted Bengal to 165 for nine and sealed a 19-run victory at the Wankhede Stadium.

sports.title: Barcelona receive €100 million offer for La Masia star amid Chelsea, Manchester United interest
sports.description: Barcelona receive €100 million offer for La Masia star amid Chelsea, Manchester United interest Even in a season where Lamine Yamal and Raphinha have attracted the limelight once again through their exceptional performances, Fermin Lopez has proven why he is such an important part of Barcelona. The Spanish international has quietly emerged as one of Barcelona’s most productive players with eight goals and seven assists in all competitions. Fermin’s brilliant season has not gone unnoticed either, with a number of Premier League clubs keen on signing the playmaker. Barcelona receive €100 million offer for Fermin Fermin has transformed into a genuine star at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) According to Diario SPORT , a host of Premier League clubs who were keen on Fermin last summer have revisited their interest in the player. In fact, Barcelona have even received an offer of around €100 million for the services of the Spanish international. Chelsea, in particular, had tabled a bid of around €70 million last summer. But it is likely that the Blues, along with other Premier League clubs such as Manchester United have tabled a bid higher than that. Chelsea and Man United are apparently the teams who have shown the most concrete interest in signing Fermin. Fermin has no desire to leave Fermin Lopez wants to remain at Barcelona. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) However, Barcelona are not worried about the prospect of Fermin Lopez leaving the club anytime shown. The player has shown no desire to leave Barcelona, even though he is a distant third behind Yamal and Raphinha, as far as the team’s biggest attacking stars are concerned. Fermin has a contract at Camp Nou until 2031, which gives the Blaugrana significant leverage even when a Premier League team does make a push to sign the player. Barcelona are also aware of Fermin’s progress and are expected to soon sit down with the player’s representative over a new contract that will likely come with a significant raise in salary. In any case, Fermin has turned deaf ears to interest from these Premier League clubs and will not consider an exit from Barcelona, no matter how lucrative an offer he gets.

sports.title: Peter Shilton reacts to Harry Kane becoming England’s most-capped player
sports.description: Photo by Carl Recine - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Peter Shilton held the record for most caps by an England player in history, earning 125 between 1970 and 1990. Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane broke that record when he made his 126th appearance in Wembley Stadium against Croatia in the UEFA Nations League, and Shilton says Kane and only Kane deserved to break his record. “I’ve held the record for quite a few years now, but if anyone deserves to overtake me, it’s Harry,” Shilton said (via FIFA as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “I couldn’t think of anyone better. sports.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
sports.description: Aryna Sabalenka will be replaced as world number two by Mirra Andreeva on Monday [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Svitolina races into WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva I hope matches between us are respected - Svitolina Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other. But Svitolina, who says she has seen the viral clips of Sabalenka's outburst on social media, says she hopes the matches between the two can be "respected". In response to Sabalenka's statement, Svitolina said on Saturday: "As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match. "We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans. I have my fans. "I just hope the matches between us [are] respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war. "It is like this in the social media, sometimes the things are turned around a little bit." Svitolina will face Mirra Andreeva in the WTA Finals showpiece after thrashing Linda Noskova in the semi-finals.
